q-124594.problem: Which of the following is equivalent to ${\int }_{C}(x+y)\,dx+(x-y)\,dy,$ where $C$ is parametrized by $r(t)=4t\,i+(4-4t)\,j$ for $t\in [0,1]?$
q-124594.worked_solution:
Along the curve, we have

$$
x(t)=4t,\,y(t)=4-4t.
$$

The derivative of $r(t)$ is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}\,i+\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}\,j \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(4t)\,i+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(4-4t)\,j \\  & =4\,i+(-4)\,j.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we can write our line integral as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{C}(x+y)\,dx+(x-y)\,dy & ={\int }_{0}^{1}(x+y)\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}\,dt+(x-y)\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}\,dt \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}((x+y)\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}+(x-y)\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t})\,dt \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}(4t+(4-4t))\cdot 4+(4t-(4-4t))\cdot (-4)\,\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}16t+16-16t-16t+16-16t\,\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}32-32t\,\text{d}t \\  & =32{\int }_{0}^{1}1-t\,\text{d}t\end{aligned}
$$

q-124868.name: Question 2
q-124868.problem: Which of the following is equivalent to ${\int }_{C}\operatorname{ln}⁡(x+y)\,dx+(x+y)\,dy,$ where $C$ is parametrized by $r(t)=i+t\,j$ for $t\in [0,2]?$
q-124868.worked_solution:
Along the curve, we have

$$
x(t)=1,\,y(t)=t.
$$

The derivative of $r(t)$ is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}\,i+\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}\,j \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(1)\,i+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(t)\,j \\  & =j.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we can write our line integral as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{C}\operatorname{ln}⁡(x+y)\,dx+(x+y)\,dy & ={\int }_{0}^{2}\operatorname{ln}⁡(x+y)\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}\,dt+(x+y)\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}\,dt \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}(\operatorname{ln}⁡(x+y)\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}+(x+y)\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t})\,dt \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}\operatorname{ln}⁡(1+t)\cdot 0+(1+t)\cdot 1\,\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}1+t\,\text{d}t\end{aligned}
$$

Question 2
?

Which of the following is equivalent to ∫Cln⁡(x+y)dx+(x+y)dy, where C is parametrized by r(t)=i+tj for t∈[0,2]?

a
∫02t+t2dt
b
∫02dt
c
∫021+tdt
d
∫02ln⁡(1+t)+t+1dt
e
∫02ln⁡(1+t)dt
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

Along the curve, we have x(t)=1,y(t)=t.

The derivative of r(t) is given by

r′(t)=dxdti+dydtj=ddt(1)i+ddt(t)j=j.

Therefore, we can write our line integral as follows:

∫Cln⁡(x+y)dx+(x+y)dy=∫02ln⁡(x+y)dxdtdt+(x+y)dydtdt=∫02(ln⁡(x+y)dxdt+(x+y)dydt)dt=∫02ln⁡(1+t)⋅0+(1+t)⋅1dt=∫021+tdt

q-124867.problem: Which of the following is equivalent to ${\int }_{C}x\,dx+{z}^{3}\,dy-{y}^{2}\,dz,$ where $C$ is a portion of the line $r(t)=\sqrt{2}t\,i+2t\,j+2t\,k$ for $t\in [1,4]?$
q-124867.worked_solution:
Along the curve, we have

$$
x(t)=\sqrt{2}t,\,y(t)=2t,\,z(t)=2t.
$$

The derivative of $r(t)$ is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}\,i+\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}\,j+\frac{\text{d}z}{\text{d}t}\,k \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\sqrt{2}t)\,i+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(2t)\,j+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(2t)\,k \\  & =\sqrt{2}\,i+2\,j+2\,k.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we can write our line integral as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{C}x\,dx+{z}^{3}\,dy-{y}^{2}\,dz & ={\int }_{1}^{4}x\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}\,dt+{z}^{3}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}\,dt-{y}^{2}\frac{\text{d}z}{\text{d}t}\,dt \\  & ={\int }_{1}^{4}(x\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}+{z}^{3}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}-{y}^{2}\frac{\text{d}z}{\text{d}t})dt \\  & ={\int }_{1}^{4}\sqrt{2}t\cdot (\sqrt{2})+8{t}^{3}\cdot (2)-4{t}^{2}\cdot (2)\,dt \\  & ={\int }_{1}^{4}16{t}^{3}-8{t}^{2}+2t\,dt\end{aligned}
$$

Which of the following is equivalent to ∫Cxdx+z3dy−y2dz, where C is a portion of the line r(t)=2ti+2tj+2tk for t∈[1,4]?

a
∫148t3−8t2+3tdt
b
∫1416t3−8t2+2tdt
c
∫144t3−4t2dt
d
∫144t4−6t2+2dt
e
∫143t3−4t2dt
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

Along the curve, we have x(t)=2t,y(t)=2t,z(t)=2t.

The derivative of r(t) is given by

r′(t)=dxdti+dydtj+dzdtk=ddt(2t)i+ddt(2t)j+ddt(2t)k=2i+2j+2k.

Therefore, we can write our line integral as follows:

∫Cxdx+z3dy−y2dz=∫14xdxdtdt+z3dydtdt−y2dzdtdt=∫14(xdxdt+z3dydt−y2dzdt)dt=∫142t⋅(2)+8t3⋅(2)−4t2⋅(2)dt=∫1416t3−8t2+2tdt

q-39681.name: Question 4
q-39681.problem: Which of the following is equivalent to ${\int }_{C}y\,dx+x\,dy+{z}^{2}\,dz,$ where $C$ is a portion of the helix $r(t)=\operatorname{cos}⁡t\,i+\operatorname{sin}⁡t\,j+t\,k$ for $t\in [0,2\pi ]?$
q-39681.worked_solution:
Along the curve, we have

$$
x(t)=\operatorname{cos}⁡t,\,y(t)=\operatorname{sin}⁡t,\,z(t)=t.
$$

The derivative of $r(t)$ is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}\,i+\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}\,j+\frac{\text{d}z}{\text{d}t}\,k \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\operatorname{cos}⁡t)\,i+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\operatorname{sin}⁡t)\,j+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(t)\,k \\  & =-\operatorname{sin}⁡t\,i+\operatorname{cos}⁡t\,j+k.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we can write our line integral as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{C}y\,dx+x\,dy+{z}^{2}\,dz & ={\int }_{0}^{2\pi }y\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}\,dt+x\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}\,dt+{z}^{2}\frac{\text{d}z}{\text{d}t}\,dt \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2\pi }(y\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}+x\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}+{z}^{2}\frac{\text{d}z}{\text{d}t})dt \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2\pi }\operatorname{sin}⁡t\cdot (-\operatorname{sin}⁡t)+\operatorname{cos}⁡t\cdot (\operatorname{cos}⁡t)+{t}^{2}\cdot 1\,dt \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2\pi }{cos}^{2}⁡t-{sin}^{2}⁡t+{t}^{2}\,dt \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2\pi }\operatorname{cos}⁡2t+{t}^{2}\,dt\end{aligned}
$$

q-90724.problem: Evaluate ${\int }_{C}-y\,dx+x\,dy+z\,dz,$ where $C$ is a portion of the helix $r(t)=\operatorname{cos}⁡t\,i+\operatorname{sin}⁡t\,j+t\,k$ for $t\in [0,2\pi ].$
q-90724.worked_solution:
Along the curve, we have

$$
x(t)=\operatorname{cos}⁡t,\,y(t)=\operatorname{sin}⁡t,\,z(t)=t.
$$

The derivative of $r(t)$ is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}\,i+\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}\,j+\frac{\text{d}z}{\text{d}t}\,k \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\operatorname{cos}⁡t)\,i+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\operatorname{sin}⁡t)\,j+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(t)\,k \\  & =-\operatorname{sin}⁡t\,i+\operatorname{cos}⁡t\,j+k.\end{aligned}
$$

We can now evaluate the line integral:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{C}-y\,dx+x\,dy+z\,dz & ={\int }_{0}^{2\pi }-y\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}\,dt+x\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}\,dt+z\frac{\text{d}z}{\text{d}t}\,dt \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2\pi }(-y\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}+x\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}+z\frac{\text{d}z}{\text{d}t})dt \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2\pi }-\operatorname{sin}⁡t\cdot (-\operatorname{sin}⁡t)+\operatorname{cos}⁡t\cdot \operatorname{cos}⁡t+t\cdot 1\,dt \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2\pi }{sin}^{2}⁡t+{cos}^{2}⁡t+t\,dt \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2\pi }1+t\,dt \\  & =(t+\frac{{t}^{2}}{2}){|}_{0}^{2\pi } \\  & =2\pi +\frac{(2\pi )^{2}}{2} \\  & =2\pi (1+\pi )\end{aligned}
$$

q-90723.problem: Evaluate ${\int }_{C}(3x+y)\,dx+x\,dy,$ where $C$ is a portion of the parabola parametrized by $r(t)={t}^{2}\,i+(4t-1)\,j$ for $t\in [0,2].$
q-90723.worked_solution:
Along the curve, we have

$$
x(t)={t}^{2},\,y(t)=4t-1.
$$

The derivative of $r(t)$ is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}\,i+\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}\,j \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({t}^{2})\,i+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(4t-1)\,j \\  & =2t\,i+4\,j.\end{aligned}
$$

We can calculate the line integral as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{C}(3x+y)\,dx+x\,dy & ={\int }_{0}^{2}(3x+y)\cdot \frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}\,dt+x\cdot \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}\,dt \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}((3x+y)\cdot \frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}+x\cdot \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t})\,dt \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}(3{t}^{2}+4t-1)\cdot 2t+{t}^{2}\cdot 4\,\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}6{t}^{3}+8{t}^{2}-2t+4{t}^{2}\,\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}6{t}^{3}+12{t}^{2}-2t\,\text{d}t \\  & ={[\frac{3}{2}{t}^{4}+4{t}^{3}-{t}^{2}]}_{0}^{2} \\  & =[\frac{3}{2}(2)^{4}+4(2)^{3}-{2}^{2}]-[0] \\  & =[24+32-4] \\  & =52\end{aligned}
$$
